THE TAHASILDHAR  SHIVAMOGGA TALUK,

 ...RESPONDENTS (BY SRI. SRIDHAR HEGDE, ADV FOR R1-R5.,ADVOCATE)
 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 & 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO-QUASH THE NOTICE OF THE R-3 DTD 15.05.2017 VIDE ANNX-L TO THIS WRIT PETITION DIRECT THE RESPONDENTS TO PAY COMPENSATION TOGETHER WITH ALL THE OTHER BENEFITS AS MANDATED UNDER THE LAND ACQUISITION ACT TOGETHER WITH UP TO DATE INTEREST FROM THE DATE OF ACQUISITION FOR ACQUIRING THE PROPERTY OF THE PETITIONER MEASURING TO AN EXTENT OF 50 FEET X 110 FEET SITUATED IN SY.NO.26/1A4 OF ALKOLA VILLAGE, KASABA HOBLI,
SHIVAMOGGA TALUK AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The essential grievance of the Petitioner is as to no compensation being paid despite his land having been acquired for a public purpose and in accordance with the due process of law.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner argues that after the acquisition, in terms of the award, the compensation was released to some other persons and on coming to know of their disentitlement, the same having been retrieved needs to be paid to his client.

He also argues that since Award Notice was not issued to his client, liberty should be reserved to him to seek enhancement of the compensation under Section 18(1) of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

2. Learned AGA appearing for the Respondents opposes the Petition contending that though the compensation was paid to wrong persons, the same having been retrieved, is now deposited before the jurisdictional Court vide LAC No.62/2018 and therefore, Petitioner can go & tap the Reference Court. The prayer for reserving right to seek enhancement of compensation does not lie because of the limitation period prescribed under Section 18(2)(b) of the 1894 Act since more than six months have expired after the award has been made.
So contending he seeks dismissal of the Writ Petition.

3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court is inclined to grant a limited indulgence in the matter as under and for the following reasons:
(a) Petitioner's land was acquired showing his name in the acquisition Notification although it was missing in the award, is demonstrably true.

The compensation was N.Krishnamurthy vs State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9085926/
2 paid to some wrong persons and the same having been retrieved has been deposited in the jurisdictional Court vide LAC No. 62/2018; the Petitioner can approach the said Court and seek withdrawal of the same by establishing his credentials,
notwithstanding that his name was missed in the Award although it figured in the Acquisition Notifications.
The Court has to consider all the contentions of the parties and decide Petitioner's claim in accordance with law, without brooking any delay.
Payment of compensation is essential when private property is acquired for public purpose, this mandate is 'in-built' in Article 300A vide K.T PLANTATION vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA (2011) 9 SCC 1.

sentences.text:
The following observations in STATE OF BIHAR vs.
MAHARAJADHIRAJA SIR KAMESHWAR SINGH (1952) SCR 889 succinctly elucidates upon the jurisprudential basis for payment of compensation as under:
"...obligation to pay compensation for the property so compulsorily acquired, is not an essential ingredient of the connotation of the term, eminent domain, but is an essential element for the valid exercise of that power payment.

MAHARAJADHIRAJA SIR KAMESHWAR SINGH (1952) SCR 889
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The obligation to pay compensation arises from the natural right of the individual who is deprived of his property by such acquisition as against the power of the Sovereign to take the property in exercise of its Sovereignty..."

(b) The second submission of learned counsel for the Petitioner that his client should be given an opportunity to seek enhancement of compensation in terms of Section 18 of the 1894 Act, has some force.
In making reference to the Court, the Collector/Land Acquisition Officer functions as a Statutory Authority and not as an agent of the Government.
When the conditions stipulated in Section 18 are fulfilled, he has no discretion not to refer the claim to the Court concerned.
He cannot come to his own conclusion that the person seeking reference is not a 'person interested' and thereby refuse to make the reference.

The right to seek reference under Section 18 of the 1894 Act is inter alia conditioned by the limitation period prescribed under sub-section (2) of Section 18 of the 1894 Act, as amended by State Amendments.
Clause (a) of this sub-section fixes a period of six weeks where award notice is sent.
Where award notice is not sent, clause (b) fixes a period of six months to himself for applying to the Reference Court.
The limitation prescribed in clause (b) is invokable where the award notice could have been sent, but remained unsent.

When the name of the interested person is missing in the Award, clause (b) of sub-section (2) of Section 18 would not become invokable inasmuch as no award notice could have been sent to such a person.

(c) In a case which does not attract of sub-clauses (a) (b) of section 18 of the erstwhile 1894 Act, the law governing limitation would be Article 137 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 which as a residuary clause prescribes a period of three years.
This period should reckon from the date of the award excluding the period spent in bona fide prosecuting the claim elsewhere, as a concession provided under Section 14 of this Act.

Since these are matters of fact, the Jurisdictional Court, if approached by the Petitioner, shall decide on his claim, taking into account the pendency of this Writ Petition during the period between 14.07.2017 N.Krishnamurthy vs State Of Karnataka on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9085926/
3 and 20.03.2023.
It is made clear that all this is relevant for staking a claim for enhancing the compensation and not for seeking the release of what has been already deposited.

If Petitioner in the background of what has been discussed hereinabove makes an appropriate application and satisfies all conditions stipulated in Section 18 of the 1894 Act, the same shall be tried & disposed off by the Reference Court within an outer limit of one year.
In the above circumstances and with the above observations, this Writ Petition is disposed off, costs having been made easy and all contentions being kept open.
